Federal regulators have fined Bank of America more than a billion dollars
for failing to take steps to prevent money laundering by its customers.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the penalty is one of the largest in Treasury Department history.
Banks are required to track and report financial transactions they suspect may be tied to illegal
activity. The Treasury Department says B of A willfully ignored that requirement and allowed
more than $5 billion worth of money to change hands without proper reporting over a seven-year
period stretching back to 2018. Some of the suspicious moves showed signs of Chinese
money laundering networks. Others had apparent ties to the southwest border. The bank also agreed
to pay more than $11 million to settle apparent sanctions violations involving Iran, Russia and
other targets. The bank says in a statement it's committed billions of dollars and thousands of
employees to improving its financial compliance. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
